report.tagline: A monthly subscription to watch films, series, games and some live events, with a cheaper plan that shows ads.
report.simpleSummary: Netflix is like a video rental shop that lives in your TV or phone. You pay every month and watch as much as you want from a big library of shows and films, many made by Netflix itself, like Squid Game or Stranger Things. It recommends what to watch next based on what you liked. There is a cheaper plan with ads, and Netflix now also streams some live events like boxing and NFL games.

overview.whatItDoes: Netflix sells monthly access to films, series, documentaries, mobile and TV games, and a growing number of live events. It spends billions on original shows from many countries and uses viewing data to recommend titles to each person. It makes money from subscriptions and, more and more, from ads on its cheaper plan.
howItWorks: Users pick a plan, from a cheaper ad-supported plan to Premium with 4K and more screens.
Each household creates profiles, and Netflix shows a different home screen for each profile.
Recommendations rank rows and even pick which thumbnail image each person sees.
Netflix licenses shows from studios and makes its own originals in over 50 countries, including India.
Since 2023, account sharing outside the household needs an 'extra member' fee in many countries.
Live events like boxing, NFL Christmas games and WWE Raw stream at set times.
overview.valueProposition: For viewers: a huge, personalised library of shows from around the world, without ads if you pay more, on any screen. For advertisers: a large, logged-in, mostly TV audience that watches with attention.

businessModel.summary: Netflix makes most of its money from monthly subscriptions, and a growing share from ads on the cheaper plan. It spends heavily on content, but that cost is shared across hundreds of millions of members, so margins keep rising. In Q3 2026 it kept about 35 cents of every dollar as operating profit.

revenueStreams.detail: Monthly plan fees, the vast majority of the $12.87 billion in Q3 2026 revenue.
Ads on the ad-supported plan and in live events, about $2.7 billion expected in 2026.
Paid sharing for people outside the household.
Smaller money from consumer products, live experiences like Netflix House, and some licensing.

businessModel.pricing: India: Mobile ₹149, Basic ₹199, Standard ₹499, Premium ₹649 a month. US (after the 2026 price rise): Standard with ads about $8.99, Standard about $19.99, Premium about $26.99 a month. Prices change often by country.
costDrivers: Content: original productions and licensed shows, about $18 billion or more a year
Streaming technology, ad tech and engineering staff
businessModel.unitEconomics: Netflix makes about $13 billion a quarter across roughly 300 million or more paying households, so it earns around $14 per household per month on average, much more in the US and much less in India. Content and other costs take about 65%, leaving about $5 of operating profit per household. The key is scale: a new member adds money but adds almost no content cost, because the same show serves everyone. An ad-plan member pays less but brings ad money on top.

howTheyGetUsers: Global hit shows that spread by word of mouth and social media
Cheaper ad plan and Mobile plan in price-sensitive markets
Bundles with telecoms like Jio and Airtel in India
Live events that pull in new viewers for one night
Paid sharing turning borrowers into members
whatBringsUsersBack: New releases every week and season drops
Personalised home screen and 'Continue watching' row
Top 10 lists that create shared talk
Live events and weekly shows like WWE Raw
growth.moat: Netflix spends more on content than almost anyone and spreads it over the biggest paying base in streaming. That lets it pay for more hits, which brings more members, a loop rivals struggle to match. Its data on what nearly 1 billion people watch helps it pick shows and recommend them.

competitors.name: YouTube
competitors.positioning: Free, creator-made video, number one on US TV screens.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Netflix sells studio-quality originals for a fee; YouTube is mostly free and creator-made.

competitors.name: Amazon Prime Video
competitors.positioning: Bundled with Prime shopping, with ads by default.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Netflix is a standalone service with more hits; Prime Video gets users through shopping.

competitors.name: Disney+ and JioHotstar
competitors.positioning: Disney brands worldwide; in India, cricket and Hindi TV with free and paid tiers.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: In India, Netflix is a premium choice without cricket; JioHotstar wins on sports and price.

competitors.name: Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery (HBO Max)
competitors.positioning: Studios with large libraries, merging after Netflix lost the Warner bid.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Netflix has more members and higher margins; the merged rival will have a deeper film and TV library.

competitors.name: Apple TV
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Netflix offers far more volume and global content.

pmLessons: Scale changes the math. A show costs the same whether 10 million or 100 million people watch, so more members means higher margins.
Pricing is a product decision. The ad plan, Mobile plan and paid sharing each opened money that a single price could not.
Removing a 'free' behaviour like password sharing can work if you give people a clear paid path.
Recommendations are about saving time. Netflix wins when members find something to watch quickly.

interviewQuestions.question: Netflix cut its ad revenue forecast. Why might that be, and what would you do?
interviewQuestions.hint: Break ad revenue into members on the ad plan, hours, ad load, fill rate and price. Find the weak link and propose fixes.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you grow Netflix in India?
interviewQuestions.hint: Look at price, telecom bundles, local content, sports gaps and payment. Compare with JioHotstar. Pick a target segment.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Netflix buy more live sports rights?
interviewQuestions.hint: Weigh new sign-ups, ad revenue and retention against rights cost and stream risk. Suggest a test like one-off events.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a feature to reduce the time people spend choosing what to watch.
interviewQuestions.hint: Define the problem with data like time to first play. Propose options, pick one, and set success and guardrail metrics.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you measure whether the password sharing crackdown succeeded?
interviewQuestions.hint: Look at net new members, extra members, churn among payers, revenue per member and customer complaints.
